How it works, end to end

What limits scale

Six findings, most serious first

The app is safe and correct for a demo and a single small business. These are the things that stop it at lakhs of cylinders, many branches or many companies.

Critical

The whole company is one JSON record

Every cylinder, order and movement lives inside one org_state row, read and rewritten on every save. Fine at 84 cylinders. At 5,00,000 cylinders and crores of movements, saves slow down and the row becomes too big to handle. Fix: one table per kind of record, with movements as an append-only table.

High

One version number for the whole company

Two people saving different things at the same moment can get "something changed, check again". On a busy dispatch morning that becomes frequent. Fix: a version per record, so only real clashes conflict.

High

Office browsers download everything at sign-in

Admin and office roles receive the full data set in one go. That is slow on 4G and will not fit in a phone's memory at scale. Fix: search, filters and pages answered by the server.

Medium

Nothing runs on a schedule

Test-due dates and rental ageing are stored, but nobody is reminded. Fix: scheduled jobs for alerts, reminders, Tally sync and nightly reports.

Medium

No place for photos or signatures

Proof of delivery is a typed name, and test certificates are a reference number. Fix: private file storage (Supabase Storage) linked to deliveries and cylinders.

Medium

One company, demo sign-in

The data model already carries a company id, but there is one company and a public demo password. A real launch needs company sign-up, staff invites, and a simple PIN or badge sign-in for workers (after a security review).

Benchmark

ctmsgas.com and us, feature by feature

ctmsgas.com sells a cylinder ERP to Indian industrial, medical and LPG gas companies. Its pitch is QR and RFID tracking, Tally and WhatsApp integration, GST billing, rental ageing and Android and iOS apps. We are ahead on the field worker's experience and behind on integrations and hardware.

Where we already lead

  • Picture-first Simple mode for workers who cannot read
  • Hindi and English with natural Sarvam voice
  • 5-second undo before anything is recorded
  • Plain-language Life story for every cylinder
  • Read a QR from a gallery photo
  • Safety rules enforced on the server, not in the screen

Brand caution: "CTMS" is their product name, and they publish trademark guidelines. Our code folder is called CTMS, but the product should launch only as Cylvero (or another name we own), never reuse their wording, and never show customer numbers we have not earned.

Roadmap

The plan, in five phases

Weeks are rough estimates for a small team of two to three developers. Phases 3 and 4 can overlap once phase 2 is done.

  1. 1. Brand and foundations

    2–3 weeks
    • Settle the name, run a trademark search, buy the domain, design the logo and colours.
    • Turn the app's styles into one design system shared by the app and the website.
    • Brand website with a demo-booking form and an ROI calculator.
    • Separate staging and production; error alerts, uptime checks and point-in-time backups.

    Done when the brand is consistent everywhere and a bad release can be caught on staging and rolled back.

  2. 2. Scale the core

    4–6 weeks
    • Move from the single JSON record to proper tables, with a one-time migration and the same rules and tests.
    • Movements become an append-only table that the database itself protects, like the audit log.
    • A version per record, server-side search and pages, and multi-company sign-up with staff invites.
    • File storage for photos, signatures and certificates; a scheduled-job runner.

    Done when a load test with 5,00,000 cylinders and 50 concurrent users keeps every save under one second.

  3. 3. Must-have integrations

    6–8 weeks
    • WhatsApp challans, invoices and reminders; SMS and email alerts.
    • Test-due and rental-ageing alerts, penalties, quotations and debit notes.
    • GST e-invoice and e-way bill; Tally sync.
    • Owner dashboards with drill-down; customer portal ("my cylinders, my bills").

    Done when an accountant can close the month without re-typing anything into Tally.

  4. 4. Field app and hardware

    6–8 weeks
    • Android and iOS app wrapping Simple mode, offline for every job, not just deliveries.
    • Signature and photo proof of delivery; Bluetooth thermal printing of challans.
    • Bluetooth UHF RFID readers and fixed gates at the filling line; GPS trips.

    Done when a driver works a full day with no network and everything syncs correctly in the evening.

  5. 5. Stand-out features

    ongoing
    • Voice commands in Hindi with Sarvam speech-to-text ("दो सिलेंडर दिए").
    • Loss and recovery predictions: which customers are holding cylinders too long.
    • WhatsApp bot for customers: "how many cylinders do I have, what do I owe".
    • More Indian languages, starting with the first customers' regions.

    Done when field workers prefer our app to paper, and owners can see losses fall month by month.

Needs the owner

Decisions before phase 1

Name and brand

Keep Cylvero, or choose another name we can trademark and get a domain for.

First market

Medical oxygen, industrial gas or LPG. LPG brings different regulations and much higher volumes.

Native app timing

Build the Android app in phase 4 as planned, or earlier if RFID and printing are must-haves for the first customers.

Partners

Which WhatsApp provider, which GST provider, and which RFID reader vendor to pilot with.

Pricing

Per cylinder, per branch, or per user. This shapes the multi-company design in phase 2.

Pilot customer

One real business to run the demo with for a month before a wider launch.
